title: Reading a search result
idea: TOOL: use the found flag with if/else to print a friendly yes/no message. Predict output.

exercises.explanation: 6 is present, so found becomes True, and the if prints 'Yes'. The flag drives a friendly message.
9 is absent, so found stays False and the else prints 'No'.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a search that prints Yes or No.
exercises.explanation: Do the found-flag search first, then an if/else on found turns the boolean into a readable message.
You test the found flag. If it is True the if runs; otherwise the else runs.

exercises.prompt: The if/else that prints Yes/No comes AFTER the search loop finishes.
exercises.explanation: You must finish checking every item before you decide. So the message comes after the loop, using the final flag.

exercises.prompt: Why not print 'Yes' inside the loop the first time you see a match?
options: You could, but if the value appears twice you would print Yes twice — the flag avoids that
exercises.explanation: A flag records the match once and you report it once, after the loop. It keeps the yes/no clean.
The list is empty, so the loop never runs and found stays False. Searching empty gives 'No' safely.

exercises.prompt: Match the final flag value to the meaning.
exercises.explanation: True means present, False means absent. An empty list can only give absent.
7 is present, so found is True and the if prints 'Found it'.

exercises.prompt: A search on an empty list is safe and simply reports 'not found'.
exercises.explanation: With no items the loop body never runs, found stays False, and you correctly report absent.
